name: Isolated Punctate Palmoplantar Keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Punctate Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of multiple discrete punctate hyperkeratotic papules on the palms and soles
No associated nail dystrophy or abnormalities
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Histological confirmation showing compact orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis without epidermolytic changes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic punctate hyperkeratotic lesions on palms and soles with histopathological confirmation; family history supportive but not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; genetic testing may be considered to exclude syndromic forms.

laboratory: Histopathology showing compact orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis without epidermolytic changes
genetic: Mutations in AAGAB gene reported in some familial cases
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic punctate keratotic papules localized to palms and soles

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of epidermolytic hyperkeratosis on histology
Larger keratotic papules with central keratin plugs

redFlags: Rapid progression of lesions with ulceration
Presence of nail dystrophy or subungual tumors
Systemic symptoms such as weight loss or lymphadenopathy
